title: MCP tool scopes must not exceed what the backend endpoint enforces (hasScopes is all-or-nothing)
answers: MCP tool missing for read-only token
alert-simulate not visible to read-only scout
Why is an MCP tool hidden from my API key catalog
tool disappears from MCP catalog instead of erroring
body:
Symptom: A read-only token (e.g. scheduled anomaly scout with alert:read + insight:read) cannot see the `alert-simulate` MCP tool at all, so it falls back to weaker raw queries.
Root cause: products/alerts/mcp/tools.yaml declared `alert:write` for alert-simulate, but AlertViewSet.simulate only enforces alert:read + insight:read. `hasScopes` in services/mcp/src/lib/api.ts requires every declared scope, so over-declaring hides the whole tool rather than gating one mode.
Fix pattern: Set `scopes:` in tools.yaml to exactly the viewset's required_scopes; leave mode-specific stricter checks (e.g. alert:write for the charged `llm` detector in `_require_write_scope_for_charged_simulation`, called from `check_throttles`) on the backend, and document them in the tool description.
Constraints: Do not hoist a single mode's requirement onto the whole tool. Keep `readOnly: false` when one mode spends money/model budget. `hasScope` treats :write as granting :read, so write-scoped callers are unaffected.
applies: products/*/mcp/tools.yaml scope declarations and the MCP tool catalog filter in services/mcp

search: MCP tool scopes declared in products/alerts/mcp/tools.yaml must match exactly what the backend endpoint enforces; `hasScopes` in services/mcp/src/lib/api.ts is all-or-nothing and hides the entire tool if any declared scope is missing. Over-declaring scopes (e.g. alert:write for `alert-simulate` when the viewset only enforces alert:read + insight:read) causes read-only tokens to lose tool access entirely, falling back to weaker raw queries. The fix pattern is to set `scopes:` to exactly what the viewset's required_scopes are and keep mode-specific stricter checks (like `_require_write_scope_for_charged_simulation`) on the backend with documentation in the tool description. Do not hoist a single mode's requirement onto the whole tool. Keep `readOnly: false` when any mode spends budget; `hasScope` treats :write as granting :read, so write-scoped callers remain unaffected. See products/alerts/mcp/tools.yaml and services/mcp/tests/unit/alert-simulate-scopes.test.ts.
